the proton solubility is reduced when the amount of Nb in the structure is increased and that the lattice parameters of the compounds are increased when the Nb content is increased.
the proton conductivity in BCN18 is significantly lower than previously reported and that the proton uptake is much smaller than previously reported.
the mixed perovskite BaCa (1+x)/3 Nb (2-x)/3 O (3-x)/2 is an ideal model system for studying the proton uptake in perovskite-type oxides.

the synthesis of a new series of mixed BaCa(1+ x ) Nb (2−x ) O 3−x /2 perovskites, with the aim of investigating the influence of the Ca content on the properties of this material.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the perovskites with x =0, x =0.12 and x =0.18 have a common structure type, while the x =0.08 and x =0,12 samples have a common crystallographic structure, but a different chemical composition.
the proton uptake in the perovskite structure of the BCN ceramics is due to the formation of O-vacancies.
BCN18 is the only mixed perovskite in this series with an extended solubility for protonic species in the lattice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BCN18 is not a proton conductor in the dry state, and that the water uptake is a consequence of a partial substitution of Ca2+ by protons, which is not possible for x <0.12.
the proton solubility in BaCa (1 + x )/3Nb (2 − x )/3O 3− x is a strong function of the Ca-content and is highest for x =0.18.
the proton conductivity of the mixed perovskite is determined by the concentration of oxygen vacancies and that the latter is controlled by the concentration of Nb in the structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proton conductivity is related to the amount of water that is incorporated into the structure, which in turn is related to the solubility of water in the ceramic.
the proton conductivity of the perovskite BCN18 is mainly determined by the proton concentration and not by the proton mobility.
the proton uptake in BCN18 is not a simple process of proton uptake into a pre-existing proton conductor.
